title: Cognitive Reframing for Perceived Overwhelm
summary: Identify cognitive distortions (catastrophizing, all-or-nothing thinking) and reframe stressful situations into manageable component tasks.
protocol: 1. Catch automatic negative thoughts when feeling overwhelmed.
2. Ask: 'What is the objective evidence for this thought?'
3. Write down a balanced, realistic alternative scenario.
4. Break the immediate stressor into a 5-minute action step.
evidence_base: American Psychological Association (APA) CBT Guidelines for Clinical Anxiety & Stress

title: Box Breathing & Vagus Nerve Stimulation
summary: 4-4-4-4 rhythm breathing protocol designed to activate the parasympathetic nervous system and increase Heart Rate Variability (HRV).
protocol: 1. Inhale deeply through the nose for 4 seconds.
2. Hold breath gently for 4 seconds.
3. Exhale fully through mouth for 4 seconds.
4. Hold empty for 4 seconds. Repeat for 5 cycles.
evidence_base: Journal of Autonomic Neuroscience (2021) - Slow Breathing & HRV Coherence

title: Circadian Synchronization & Non-Sleep Deep Rest (NSDR)
summary: Restorative protocol to improve sleep efficiency and reduce nighttime cortisol spikes.
protocol: 1. Get 10-15 minutes of direct sunlight within 1 hour of waking.
2. Discontinue caffeine consumption at least 8 hours prior to sleep.
3. Keep bedroom temperature cool (65-68°F / 18-20°C).
4. Perform a 10-minute guided NSDR / Yoga Nidra scan if awake in bed.
evidence_base: Sleep Medicine Reviews - Behavioral Interventions for Stress-Induced Insomnia

title: Pomodoro Ultradian Rhythm & Micro-Rest Breaks
summary: Structures intense focus into 90-minute ultradian cycles followed by non-screen micro-rests to prevent cognitive exhaustion.
protocol: 1. Work in focused 50-minute blocks followed by a 10-minute non-screen break.
2. Stand up, stretch, look at objects 20+ feet away to relax visual accommodation.
3. Limit total daily continuous screen exposure without breaks.
4. Establish a hard end-of-workday shutdown ritual.
evidence_base: Ergonomics Journal - Micro-breaks and Occupational Mental Fatigue

title: Aerobic Somatic Tension Release
summary: Moderate aerobic movement to metabolize excess stress hormones (cortisol, adrenaline) and boost endorphins.
protocol: 1. Perform 20-30 minutes of zone-2 cardio (brisk walking, light cycling, swimming).
2. Focus on somatic sensations rather than performance metrics.
3. Perform progressive muscle relaxation (PMR) post-exercise.
evidence_base: Harvard Medical School - Exercise and Stress Neurobiology

title: Mindful Body Scan & Emotional Labeling
summary: Reduces amygdala hyper-reactivity by non-judgmentally observing bodily sensations and labeling emotions accurately.
protocol: 1. Sit comfortably and scan body from toes to head for physical tension.
2. Name the emotion ('I am noticing a feeling of anxiety/frustration').
3. Observe without trying to force immediate change.
4. Breathe into areas of physical tightness.
evidence_base: NeuroImage - Affect Labeling Mitigates Limbic Reactivity

title: Cool-Down Protocol for Anger & Irritability
summary: Immediate physiological de-escalation for facial expressions signalling anger, using paced exhalation and cognitive distancing.
protocol: 1. Stop what you are doing and stand or sit with both feet grounded.
2. Inhale for 2 counts, exhale for 6 counts (longer exhalation calms the fight-or-flight response).
3. Repeat 6-8 cycles while clenching and releasing fists.
4. Ask: 'Will this matter in 24 hours?' then choose a response, not a reaction.
evidence_base: Frontiers in Psychology - Anger Management & Slow Breathing Interventions

title: Grounding & Worry Containment for Fear
summary: 5-4-3-2-1 sensory grounding to interrupt the fear spiral detected in facial expressions, followed by scheduled worry time.
protocol: 1. Name 5 things you can see, 4 you can touch, 3 you can hear, 2 you can smell, 1 you can taste.
2. Place both palms on a solid surface and press firmly for 10 seconds.
3. Write the fear down and schedule a 15-minute 'worry window' later today.
4. During the worry window, problem-solve only what is within your control.
evidence_base: Journal of Anxiety Disorders - Grounding Techniques for Panic & Fear

title: Behavioural Activation for Low Mood
summary: Counteracts sadness detected via facial analysis with small, rewarding activities that rebuild behavioural momentum.
protocol: 1. Schedule one tiny pleasant activity today (10 minutes, e.g. walk outdoors, phone a friend).
2. Pair it with an achievement activity (tidying one shelf, one email).
3. Notice and log how your mood shifts 15 minutes afterwards.
4. Repeat tomorrow; stack two activities once one feels easy.
evidence_base: Behaviour Research & Therapy - Behavioural Activation for Depression & Sadness

title: Sensory Downtime After Overstimulation
summary: For surprise-driven arousal spikes, a structured sensory reset reduces cognitive load and stabilizes stress hormones.
protocol: 1. Step away from screens for 10 minutes.
2. Dim lighting, silence or low ambient sound, and slow, rhythmic breathing.
3. Drink water and take three long, sighing breaths.
4. Return to the task with a single clear priority.
evidence_base: International Journal of Environmental Research & Public Health - Digital Detox & Arousal Regulation

title: Somatic Release for Disgust & Tension
summary: Addresses the tension and revulsion response signalled by disgust expressions through progressive muscle relaxation.
protocol: 1. Tense each muscle group (jaw, shoulders, fists) for 5 seconds, then release fully.
2. Move from head to feet, noticing the difference between tension and relaxation.
3. Take 3 slow breaths, exhaling through pursed lips.
4. Refocus attention on a pleasant, neutral sensory detail in the room.
evidence_base: Applied Psychophysiology & Biofeedback - Progressive Muscle Relaxation Efficacy

title: Savoring & Positive Emotion Amplification
summary: When facial analysis detects happiness, capitalize on it: savoring lengthens positive affect and builds resilience.
protocol: 1. Pause and deliberately notice the positive moment for 30 seconds.
2. Share it with someone or write it down in one sentence.
3. Reflect on what made it possible and plan a similar micro-moment tomorrow.
4. Use the positive state to attempt one moderate challenge.
evidence_base: Journal of Positive Psychology - Savoring and Subjective Well-Being
